charts.title: Sales Over Time
charts.description: Chronological progression of sales aggregated by order_id.

analyticalExplanation.summary: This time-series tracks sales across 20 chronological periods from 1001-01-01 to 1020-01-01.
keyObservations: Peak volume reached on 1012-01-01 with 3,200 in total.
Overall trajectory indicates stable operational continuity.
potentialDrivers: Seasonal purchasing cycles and month-end closing activities.
Marketing campaigns or promotional schedule spikes.
suggestedInvestigation: Examine transaction records for peak date 1012-01-01 to isolate contributing orders.
Compare weekday vs weekend volume distribution.
analyticalExplanation.metricDefinition: Daily aggregate: SUM(sales) grouped by truncated order_id.

charts.title: Sales by Region
charts.description: Comparison of cumulative sales across top 4 segments of region.

analyticalExplanation.summary: Shows distribution of sales across distinct region groups.
keyObservations: Top contributing segment is "North America" generating 7,292.99 (74.9% of total).
The difference between the highest and lowest top category is 6,853.49.
potentialDrivers: Market demand density and premium product positioning in top segment.
suggestedInvestigation: Audit product margin variations within "North America".
Identify opportunities to replicate success in lower-performing categories.
analyticalExplanation.metricDefinition: SUM(sales) grouped by region, sorted descending.

charts.title: Distribution of Region
charts.description: Proportional breakdown of records by region.

analyticalExplanation.summary: Illustrates the relative proportion of observations classified by region.
keyObservations: Primary share belongs to "North America" representing 9 records.
Top 2 groups comprise 70% of the total dataset.
potentialDrivers: Natural customer demographic grouping or operational default classifications.
suggestedInvestigation: Cross-tabulate region against financial metrics to verify profitability per segment.

charts.title: Quantity vs. Sales
charts.description: Bivariate correlation plot showing relationship between sales and quantity (Pearson r = -0.35).

analyticalExplanation.summary: Assesses linear dependency between sales and quantity. The sample correlation coefficient is r = -0.35.
keyObservations: Scatter points demonstrate normal dispersion across primary operating ranges.
potentialDrivers: Direct pricing-volume elasticity or scale efficiencies.
suggestedInvestigation: Segment scatter points by category to test for subgroup interaction effects.
